narrative.storylet.ratsInTheStores.title: Rats in the Stores
narrative.storylet.ratsInTheStores.text: The reeve of {holdingName} comes to your high seat holding a sack at arm’s length. Inside is the gnawed corner of a grain-bin, and a smell. “The cats have gone soft,” he says, “or the rats have gone bold. Either way the barley is feeding the wrong mouths, and it is a long while to harvest.”
narrative.storylet.ratsInTheStores.cats: Buy hunting cats from the next trader ({catCost} silver)
−{catCost} silver. Loyalty in {holdingName} +3. The granary-wives approve.
narrative.storylet.ratsInTheStores.hunt: Hold a rat-hunt, with a feast for whoever brings the most tails ({feastCost} silver)
−{feastCost} silver. Loyalty +6, Renown +1. Loud, lucky and long remembered.
{rulerName} held a rat-hunt at {holdingName}, with a feast for the best of the hunters. The tally of tails was disputed for years.
narrative.storylet.ratsInTheStores.seal: Have the bins sealed with clay and tar
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.title: The Wandering Stone
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.text: Two farmers of {holdingName} stand before you, mud to the knee and grievance to the eyebrows. Between their fields stood a boundary stone. It still stands, says old Ulfar — ten paces into his barley, and it did not walk there by itself. Young Brodd says stones settle. The whole hall is enjoying this enormously.
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.elder: Rule for Ulfar: the stone goes back, and Brodd pays {fine} silver
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.elder.p: +{fine} silver, Honor +2. Brodd’s kin will mutter (loyalty −1).
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.split: Split the strip and tell them to share the barley
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.split.p: Neither man is pleased, which is how you know it is fair. Loyalty +2.
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.lift: Make them both hold the stone overhead; the first to drop it loses
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.lift.pr: The hall will talk of nothing else for a season. Renown +2, loyalty +1.
narrative.storylet.boundaryStone.lift.ch: At {holdingName}, {rulerName} settled a boundary quarrel by making both farmers hold the stone aloft. Ulfar won by the length of a sneeze.
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.title: A Boast in the Cups
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.text: You wake with a mouth like a tar-barrel and a hall full of people who remember last night better than you do. Somewhere between the fourth horn and the sixth, it seems, you swore before witnesses to swim the Gray Firth before the ice goes out. The skald has already found a rhyme for it.
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.swear.pr: Renown +3 now. The Firth will want its answer within the month.
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.laugh: Laugh it off — everyone boasts at Yule
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.laugh.pr: Renown −2, Honor −1. Some will remember that you laughed.
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.bribe: Pay the skald {bribe} silver to find a different rhyme
narrative.storylet.drunkenBoast.bribe.pr: −{bribe} silver, Honor −2. Skalds talk, even the paid ones.
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.title: The Firth Remembers
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.text: The day has come. Half your folk line the shore below {capitalName}, stamping against the cold. The water is the colour of an old blade. Your hirdmaster has brought a rope, a fire and an opinion, and he shares all three before anyone asks.
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.swim: Swim it — you were raised in colder water
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.swim.c: {rulerName} swam the Gray Firth in winter to make good a Yule boast, and came out of the water asking for ale.
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.rope: Swim it, and trust the hirdmaster’s rope
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.rope.p: Renown +5, Honor +2. You will be hauled out blue, but you will be hauled out.
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.rope.c: {rulerName} made good a Yule boast in the Gray Firth and was dragged out on a rope, still swimming.
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.void: Declare the ice unsafe and the oath void
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.void.p: Honor −4, Renown −5. The skald keeps his rhyme.
narrative.storylet.boastReckoning.void.c: {rulerName} looked at the Gray Firth in winter and found a reason not to swim it. The skald found a rhyme for that too.
narrative.storylet.ravenOverTheWake.text: For two days a raven has kept pace with your ships, riding the wind off the stern and settling on the yard whenever the oars rest. The crew swear it is the Hooded Wanderer’s own bird, sent to see what you are made of. The cook, who tips the fish guts over the side each evening, has his own theory and keeps it to himself.
narrative.storylet.ravenOverTheWake.feed: Throw it a share of the salt fish
Favor of Valgrim +2. Ten rations to a bird.
narrative.storylet.ravenOverTheWake.seer: Let the rune-seer read its flight
Favor of Valgrim +1. The seer will say something; seers always do.
The seer watches the raven turn twice above the mast. “It goes where we go,” she says at last, “and it is not hungry.” The crew decide that is a fine omen. The cook says nothing.
narrative.storylet.ravenOverTheWake.shoo: Shoo it off — ravens are for the dead
Dread +1, Favor of Valgrim −2. The crew will mutter at the oars.
narrative.storylet.afterTheShieldWall.te: The noise goes out of the day all at once. Men sit where they stand. Someone is laughing who should not be, and someone is quiet who should be laughing. Your skald picks his way between the dropped shields with a wax tablet, already counting what can be sung.
narrative.storylet.afterTheShieldWall.wo: Honor +2. The skald can wait; he will anyway.
narrative.storylet.afterTheShieldWall.sk: Hear the skald’s draft now, while it is hot
A verse travels further than a ship.
narrative.storylet.afterTheShieldWall.pl: Count the plunder before the lieutenants do
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.title: The Skald’s Draft
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.text: “I have the shape of it,” says the skald, scratching at the wax. “But a verse carries only so much, {rulerSex, select, female {lady} other {lord}}. Do they remember the blood, or the ones who bled? The fallen, or your own name? Choose, and I will make it stick for a hundred winters.”
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.slaughter: After the fight the skald made a verse of the slaughter. It was sung in halls that had never heard of the battle, and they shuddered.
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.fallen: Sing of the fallen, every name
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.fallen.ch: After the fight the skald made a verse that named every one of the fallen. Their kin learned it by heart.
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.self.prev: Renown +5, Honor −1. Modesty is for farmers.
narrative.storylet.skaldsDraft.self.chro: After the fight the skald made a verse about {rulerName}, and only about {rulerName}. It was a very good verse.
narrative.notify.inbox: {count, plural, one {A matter waits} other {# matters wait}} for you in the Affairs of State.
narrative.notify.delegated: Your steward settled a matter in your name.
narrative.notify.expired: Left waiting too long, a matter was settled by your steward.
narrative.notify.lapsed: A matter that waited for you no longer needs an answer.
narrative.notify.failed: A matter could not be settled as ordered; your steward did what could be done.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.sparks: Mind the sparks. Everything in here is hot, sharp, or both.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.axeHeads: You’ve come about axe-heads. Everyone comes about axe-heads.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.hands: Stand where the light’s good. I like to see a customer’s hands before I name a price.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.cheapIron: Iron’s cheap this season and charcoal cheaper. Ask me for something difficult.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.pots: I’m mending pots for barley these days. Show me silver and I’ll remember how to make a sword.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.famous: Your name reached my anvil before you did. Half the district wants a blade like yours.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.youngJarl: Young for the high seat. Your grip will catch up with your title — I can help it along.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.warmth: Come in out of the cold. Best warmth in the district, and I only charge for the iron.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.dread: Your order will be done quick. Very quick. No need to wait about.
narrative.line.smith.greeting.yourForge: Your forge, your iron, your smith. My prices, though.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.wetBench: Sit anywhere that isn’t wet. The ale is brown and the news is fresh, and one of those is true.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.seaChappe: Another sea-chapped face. Bench by the fire, and I’ll bring something that was ale once.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.outside: If you’re here to fight, do it outside. If you’re here to drink, you’re in the right house.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.fatPurses: Busy night. Merchants with fat purses — talk to them before they’re drunk enough to lie.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.thinAle: Thin times. The ale’s thin too, but it’s wet, and I’ll take your silver for it.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.snow: Shut that door before the snow takes a seat.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.sungBadly: I know that face. A skald sang you here last week. Badly, but he sang you.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.farFromHo: You’re a long way from your own fires. The ale won’t make you homesick, at least.
narrative.line.keeper.greeting.payFirst: Pay first. Nothing personal. Well — everything personal.
narrative.verse.yearEnd.open.turned: Hear me, hall-folk: the year {year} has turned its last, and grey runs {seaKenning}.
narrative.verse.yearEnd.open.spent: The year {year} is spent like silver from a purse. Hear what {rulerKenning} bought with it.
narrative.verse.yearEnd.close.benches: So the year ends. Now comes {winterKenning}; the benches keep the tale.
narrative.verse.yearEnd.close.horns: Fill the horns. What was done is done, and now it is sung.
narrative.verse.epitaph.open.gulls: Here lies {name}, {rulerKenning}, who heard the gulls cry over {seaKenning}.
narrative.verse.epitaph.open.stone: Raise the stone for {name}, and let the carver cut it deep.
narrative.verse.epitaph.close.quieter: Now {name} has gone to {deathKenning}. The hall is quieter, and the song is longer.
narrative.verse.epitaph.close.ashes: Cold the ashes, warm the telling: {name} is not forgotten.
narrative.verse.epitaph.close.tier0: No stone was raised for {name}; nothing remembers oars on {seaKenning}.
narrative.verse.epitaph.close.tier4: At dusk came {carrion} to the hall of {name}; the seat at the long table was already warm.
narrative.verse.deed.battle.stood: At {place} ran {bloodKenning}; {warriorKenning} stood, and the foe did not.
narrative.verse.deed.battle.plain: There was {battleKenning}, and the skald was there to see it.
narrative.verse.deed.raid.heavier: Over {seaKenning} to {place}; {fireKenning} woke, and the chests came home heavier.
narrative.verse.deed.raid.lowInWater: At dawn the keel touched {place}; by noon {shipKenning} sat low in the water.
narrative.verse.deed.duel.spoke: Hand to hand with {foe}: {swordKenning} spoke, and {foe} had no answer.
narrative.verse.deed.duel.plain: Within the hazel-stakes, {swordKenning} settled the matter.
narrative.verse.deed.voyage.farAs: Out over {seaKenning} rode {shipKenning}, as far as {place}, and home again to tell it.
narrative.verse.deed.voyage.plain: Far went the oars over {seaKenning}, and the skald counted the miles.
narrative.verse.deed.marriage.handTaken: Then {goldKenning} was given and a hand was taken: {name} wed {spouse}.
narrative.verse.deed.birth.named: A child cried in the longhouse; {child} was named, and {rulerKenning} smiled.
narrative.verse.deed.death.room: {deceased} went to {deathKenning}, and the benches made room for grief.
narrative.verse.deed.relic.looked: {relic} came to the hall, and men looked at the hall differently.
narrative.verse.deed.crown.circlet: A crown for {name}: {crown}, and {goldKenning} to go with it.
narrative.verse.deed.thing.nodded: At the Thing the law-words went {name}’s way, and even the old men nodded.
narrative.verse.deed.feud.answered: The feud with {foe} was answered; {bloodKenning} was paid in kind.
narrative.verse.deed.default.meter: Much else was done that the skald has not yet set to meter.
